subject: deer ked fly
title: This Fly Lands on a Deer and Snaps Off Its Own Wings

scenes.text: This fly flies exactly once in its life. Then it throws its wings away.
The deer ked hunts for a deer, lands in its fur, and breaks off both wings for good.
From then on it lives there, crawling and drinking blood.
A 2026 study found something stranger: once it lands, its vision genes drop to about half their activity.
In the dark of the fur, sight is no longer worth the cost.
No wings, dimmer eyes. It gives up flying and seeing for one deer, forever.

description:
Deer keds (Lipoptena) are blood-sucking flies that fly to find a deer, land, then shed their wings and live in the fur.
A 2026 study in the Journal of Experimental Biology (Aberystwyth University) found the activity of their vision genes (opsins) falls to about half once they have settled on a host.
Would you rather have this fly's life or a mosquito's?
thumbnail_text: IT SNAPS OFF ITS OWN WINGS
first_comment: It flies once, then never again. Which parasite has the strangest life cycle you've heard of?
